text: One song is played at every wedding in your nation. What is it about, and why do the grandparents wince?
Your coins carry a face or a symbol that people argue about. What is it, and who wants it replaced?
Does your nation have conscription? Say who serves, who gets out of it, and how.
Your second city insists it should be the first. What does it have that the capital doesn't?
What do people in your nation queue for without complaint, and what would start a riot if they had to queue for it?
A civil servant has held the same desk for forty years and outlasted eleven ministers. What do they know?
A region of your nation votes against the government every single time. What does it want that it never gets?
Your nation once lost a war it still calls a draw. What did the peace really cost?
Your national dish started as poor people's food. What is in it, and who serves the expensive version now?
There is something your nation has to import and hates importing. What is it, and who sells it?
Your army's most decorated regiment is recruited from a single region. Why there, and what does the region expect in return?
There is a corner of your nation that every map shows and almost nobody visits. What is out there, and who lives there anyway?
A child in your nation turns sixteen. What are they suddenly allowed to do, and what is still three years away?
Name the journalist your government fears most. What story are they sitting on?
Your head of state has one power they have never dared to use. What would have to happen first?
An old family name still opens doors in your nation. What did that family do, and how long ago?
A sport nobody else takes seriously fills stadiums in your nation. Which rule does a foreigner never understand?
A town in your nation was built around one industry, and the industry has just closed. What happens to the town?
Your nation keeps a military base far from home. What deal put it there, and who thinks it was a bad one?
A mountain pass, a strait or a bridge: pick the one place your nation cannot afford to lose. What happens on the day it closes?
A border town speaks a different language from the capital. How did that happen?
Your navy's oldest ship is retired. Who wants to keep it afloat?
Name a holiday only your nation celebrates, and the food that goes with it.
A trade route your nation depends on closes overnight. What do people buy instead?
Your nation's capital moved two centuries ago. Why, and who still resents it?
Your parliament has a rule everyone agrees is absurd and nobody will repeal. What is it, and who does it quietly protect?
Every schoolchild in your nation learns one date by heart. What happened then, and which part do the textbooks leave out?
Visitors to your nation always commit the same breach of manners. What is it, and how do the locals let them know?
One company employs so many people that your government asks it before deciding anything. What does it make, and what does it get away with?
Your armed forces keep one tradition that makes no military sense at all. What is it, and what happened the last time someone tried to end it?
One river in your nation floods every few years, and people keep living beside it. What keeps them there?
It is seven in the morning in your nation. What is breakfast, how do people get to work, and what is everyone complaining about?
Your nation's most trusted public figure is not a politician. Who are they, and what would it take to ruin them?
One ministry in your government is where careers go to die. Which one, and what did the last minister do to be sent there?
There is a statue in your capital that half the country would like taken down. Who is it of, and why is it still standing?
